El Banco Central Europeo empieza a revertir parte del camino recorrido en los últimos años.  Entre junio de 2024 y junio de 2025, la facilidad de depósito —uno de los principales tipos de referencia del BCE— descendió desde el 4,00% hasta el 2,00%. Desde ese mínimo, dos aumentos de 25 puntos básicos la han situado en el 2,50%, con efecto desde el 16 de septiembre de 2026. El cambio acumulado es todavía limitado frente a los 200 puntos básicos recorridos durante la fase anterior, pero modifica la dirección observada en la serie: los dos últimos movimientos efectivos han sido subidas de tipos. En su decisión de septiembre, el BCE vinculó dicho aumento a unas perspectivas de inflación todavía elevadas y reiteró que continuará evaluando la orientación de la política monetaria reunión a reunión, sin comprometerse de antemano con una senda concreta.  Tras dos subidas consecutivas, la dirección del movimiento ha cambiado. La cuestión ahora es si este giro terminará siendo una excepción o el comienzo de una nueva etapa para la política monetaria europea. Síguenos y mantente al día con el gráfico de la semana.

Crude oil is becoming relevant for bond markets once again. In recent months, the rise in WTI (West Texas Intermediate) crude prices has coincided at times with higher yields on the U.S. 10-year Treasury, while the 14-day correlation between the two assets has remained positive during several periods. The relationship is not automatic, but it is relevant: when energy prices rise, markets may reassess inflation expectations, monetary policy, and risk premia. For investors, oil matters not only because of its impact on commodities. It can also influence expectations for interest rates, bonds, and asset valuations. The question is: Is energy regaining prominence among the factors shaping financial markets? Follow us and keep up with our chart of the week

El crudo vuelve a ser relevante para el mercado de bonos. En los últimos meses, el repunte del crudo WTI (West Texas Intermediate) ha coincidido en algunos periodos con una subida de la TIR del bono estadounidense a 10 años, mientras la correlación a 14 días entre ambos activos se ha mantenido en terreno positivo en varios episodios. La lectura no es automática, pero sí relevante: cuando la energía se encarece, el mercado puede reevaluar inflación, política monetaria y primas de riesgo. Para los inversores, el petróleo no solo importa por su impacto en materias primas. También puede condicionar expectativas de tipos, bonos y valoración de activos. La pregunta es: ¿Está recuperando la energía protagonismo entre los factores que influyen en los mercados? Síguenos y manténte al día con el gráfico de la semana

Ahora, tras el anuncio de un acuerdo entre EEUU e Irán, el precio del Brent ha corregido con fuerza, reflejando una menor percepción de riesgo de interrupciones en el suministro. Aquí me surge una duda. Si el acuerdo se ha anunciado el día 15 de junio, no ha dado mucho tiempo a la corrección del precio del barril, ¿no? Viendo la evolución, viene cayendo el precio desde el inicio del mes de junio, no sé si porque el mercado lo descontaba o por otros motivos.   El gráfico muestra cómo el petróleo reacciona de forma abrupta no solo a los shocks de oferta, sino también a la percepción de que esos riesgos puedan normalizarse.   Para los mercados, la inflación y los bancos centrales, seguir la evolución del precio del crudo sigue siendo clave.   La pregunta es si esta corrección marca un cambio de tendencia… o solo una pausa en la volatilidad geopolítica. Now, following the announcement of an agreement between the U.S. and Iran, Brent prices have corrected significantly, reflecting a lower perceived risk of supply disruptions. The chart shows how oil reacts abruptly not only to supply shocks, but also to the perception that those risks may normalize. For markets, inflation, and central banks, monitoring the evolution of oil prices remains key. The question is whether this correction marks a change in trend… or merely a pause in geopolitical volatility. Follow us and keep up with our chart of the week

La IA no solo necesita más capacidad de cómputo. También necesita mucha más energía.   Según la Agencia Internacional de la Energía, la potencia que requieren los servidores de IA se multiplicó por 11 entre 2020 y 2025 y podría volver a cuadruplicarse de aquí a 2027. Para ponerlo en perspectiva: un único conjunto de servidores (rack) de última generación podría llegar a demandar tanta potencia como 65 hogares. A menudo hablamos de la velocidad a la que avanza la IA, pero detrás de cada nuevo modelo hay una infraestructura física y energética cada vez más exigente.   La pregunta es: ¿qué será más determinante para el futuro de la IA, la innovación tecnológica o la capacidad de la infraestructura para sostenerla? The European Central Bank is beginning to reverse part of the path it has taken in recent years. Between June 2024 and June 2025, the deposit facility, one of the ECB’s key policy rates, fell from 4.00% to 2.00%. Since reaching that low, two 25 basis point increases have brought it to 2.50%, effective from 16 September 2026. The cumulative change remains limited compared with the 200 basis points covered during the previous phase, but it alters the direction observed in the series: the last two effective moves have been rate hikes. In its September decision, the ECB linked the increase to inflation expectations that remain elevated and reiterated that it will continue to assess the stance of monetary policy on a meeting-by-meeting basis, without committing in advance to any specific path. After two consecutive rate hikes, the direction of the trend has changed. The question now is whether this shift will ultimately prove to be an exception or the beginning of a new phase for European monetary policy. Follow us and keep up with our chart of the week.

¿Por qué la gasolina no ha bajado si el petróleo sí lo ha hecho desde los máximos de abril?  Una parte importante de la explicación reside en la evolución de los márgenes de refino: el diferencial entre el precio del barril de crudo y el de los productos finales, como diésel o gasolina, se sitúa en niveles históricamente elevados. Esta evolución responde, entre otros elementos, al daño en infraestructura refinera en Oriente Próximo, ciertas restricciones puntuales de exportación, la oferta mundial limitada de refinados y una demanda sólida de combustibles. Este episodio ilustra cómo determinados cuellos de botella en las cadenas de suministro pueden influir en variables macroeconómicas como la inflación o la renta disponible Síguenos y mantente al día con el gráfico de la semana.

Why haven't gasoline prices fallen if crude oil has retreated from its April highs? A key part of the answer lies in refining margins: the spread between the price of crude oil and refined products such as gasoline and diesel remains at historically elevated levels. This reflects, among other factors, damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East, temporary export restrictions, limited global supply of refined products, and strong fuel demand. This episode highlights how supply chain bottlenecks can influence broader macroeconomic variables such as inflation and disposable income.   Follow us and keep up with our chart of the week.

The aggregate data tells only part of the story. Public debt in the euro area reached 88.9% of GDP in the first quarter of 2026, but that average masks wide dispersion: from 143.5% in Greece and 138.9% in Italy to 64.4% in Germany and 37% in Ireland. Spain stood at 101.6%, one point higher than at the end of 2025, but 1.7 points lower than a year earlier. The difference matters: countries with lower relative debt would, in principle, have greater room to deploy fiscal stimulus or additional public investment. Even so, debt sustainability also depends on growth, financing costs, and the maturity profile. Which variable should matter most: debt, growth, or fiscal room? El dato agregado cuenta solo una parte de la historia.   La deuda pública de la zona Euro alcanzó el 88,9% del PIB en el primer trimestre de 2026, pero esa media oculta una amplia dispersión: del 143,5% de Grecia y el 138,9% de Italia al 64,4% de Alemania y el 37% de Irlanda. España se situó en el 101,6%, un punto más que al cierre de 2025, pero 1,7 puntos menos que un año antes.   La diferencia importa: los países con menor deuda relativa partirían, en principio, de un margen más amplio para desplegar estímulos fiscales o inversión pública adicional. Aun así, la sostenibilidad de la deuda depende también del crecimiento, el coste de financiación y el calendario de vencimientos.   ¿Qué variable debería pesar más: deuda, crecimiento o margen fiscal? AI doesn't just need chips. It also needs electricity. According to the IEA, global electricity consumption from data centres reached approximately 415 TWh in 2024 and could rise to around 945 TWh by 2030. To put that into perspective, the 2024 figure is equivalent to nearly three times the annual electricity sold to end customers across New York State. This represents a significant increase. However, it's important to keep it in context: even by 2030, data centres would still account for less than 3% of global electricity consumption. Os mercados globais permaneceram atentos à trajetória dos juros, com dados de atividade resilientes nos Estados Unidos reforçando expectativas de uma política monetária mais restritiva. Na Europa, preocupações fiscais e inflacionárias seguiram pressionando as taxas de títulos públicos, enquanto a China trouxe sinais mais positivos com novas medidas de estímulo à economia.  No Brasil, o mercado de trabalho seguiu resiliente em agosto, mas o mercado de crédito segue indicando arrefecimento da economia. Dados fiscais indicam que o governo pode cumprir a meta de resultado primário do ano, embora a dívida pública siga em trajetória ascendente. A combinação de desaceleração gradual da atividade e expectativas de continuidade do ciclo de flexibilização monetária sustentou um desempenho relativamente melhor dos ativos locais, em meio ao acompanhamento das perspectivas fiscais e econômicas para os próximos anos. A volatilidade do petróleo e os dados positivos nos Estados Unidos e na Zona do Euro reforçaram as expectativas de aperto monetário pelo Fed e pelo BCE, pressionando os juros futuros globais.  No Brasil, o Banco Central reconheceu sinais de desaceleração da atividade e não fechou as portas para mais um corte na Selic, mas manteve uma postura cautelosa diante dos riscos inflacionários, fiscais e externos. AI doesn’t just need more computing power. It also needs much more energy. According to the International Energy Agency, the power required by AI servers increased elevenfold between 2020 and 2025 and could quadruple again by 2027. To put this into perspective, a single next-generation server rack could require as much power as 65 households. We often talk about the speed at which AI is advancing, but behind every new model lies an increasingly demanding physical and energy infrastructure. The question is: what will be more decisive for the future of AI, technological innovation or the ability of infrastructure to support it? Follow us and keep up with our chart of the week.

As decisões de política monetária dominaram a semana e reforçaram a divergência entre os ciclos econômicos de Estados Unidos e Brasil. O Federal Reserve elevou os juros e adotou uma comunicação mais cautelosa, sinalizando preocupação com a persistência da inflação em um ambiente de atividade ainda resiliente. Dados de consumo acima do esperado e a alta recente dos preços de energia reforçam a avaliação de que o processo de desinflação segue sujeito a riscos, mantendo a expectativa de juros elevados por mais tempo.  No Brasil, o Copom deu continuidade ao ciclo de flexibilização monetária, em linha com a desaceleração gradual da atividade e a melhora da composição da inflação. Indicadores recentes apontam perda de fôlego do crescimento, enquanto as medidas subjacentes de preços seguem comportamento mais favorável. Ainda assim, o cenário externo mais desafiador e as incertezas domésticas recomendam cautela, deixando em aberto o ritmo e o momento dos próximos movimentos da política monetária. Confira a análise de Priscila Deliberalli, nossa Head de Economia, no Private View desta semana. #economia #juros #fed

For investors, this serves as a reminder that investing in more than 500 stocks does not necessarily mean that risk is distributed in the same proportion: the performance of a small group of large companies now has a considerable influence on the index as a whole. Long-term U.S. debt continues to require higher yields. The increase in long-term yields is not driven solely by the term premium; it also appears to reflect higher expectations for short-term interest rates. This chart helps put more than just a single figure into context: it shows a persistent trend, a term premium higher than in previous years, and a cost of financing that continues to warrant attention. Crude oil is becoming relevant for bond markets once again. In recent months, the rise in WTI (West Texas Intermediate) crude prices has coincided at times with higher yields on the U.S. 10-year Treasury, while the 14-day correlation between the two assets has remained positive during several periods. The relationship is not automatic, but it is relevant: when energy prices rise, markets may reassess inflation expectations, monetary policy, and risk premia. For investors, oil matters not only because of its impact on commodities. It can also influence expectations for interest rates, bonds, and asset valuations.
